messages:
ana (PM): quick sync — we need to pick a prioritization path for Q2 pricing work. options: 1) tiered rate caps + soft quotas 2) reserved (committed) pools with SLA 3) hybrid commit + burst credits. thoughts?
jordan (sales): customers keep asking for reserved capacity + predictable billing. mid-market deals fall apart without commit options.
sarah (finance): +1 for reserved from revenue predictability POV but it adds churn risk if commit tiers are mispriced. we need guardrails.
mike (eng): reserved means more runtime complexity: dedicated pools, routing, pre-warm. Hybrid (commit + burst) could reuse existing routing but needs fairshare.
nana (ops-bot): new incident template: reserved-pool-fallback created.
kevin (devex): dev experience note: onboarding reserved should be as self-serve as possible. customers hate manual ops. can we automate pool binding in console?
nana (ops-bot): deploy-bot: feature-flag reserve-pools rollout gated to 20% orgs.
nana (ops-bot): lint: remember to add metrics for "commit_utilization" and "burst_cost".
nana (ana): quick RICE attempt: Reach = handful of mid-market deals (score 6), Impact = high for renewal (8), Confidence = medium (5), Effort = backend+billing+console (8). rough total = ? (we can compute later).
jordan (sales): ROI case: if commit reduces price by 25% vs on-demand but guarantees capacity, legal + procurement are happier. big tenants prefer 12mo commits.
mike (eng): engineering ask breakdown: routing + capacity (4 wks), autoscaler changes (3 wks), billing plumbing (2 wks), console UI (2 wks). can parallelize but not fully.
sarah (finance): billing edge case: we need prorated credits, unused commit refunds? suggest non-refundable credits with rollover up to 3 months.
kevin (devex): UX criteria for launch: 1) self-serve purchase, 2) clear UIs for utilization and wasted commit, 3) docs + quickstart. If any missing, sales shouldn't promise.
nana (ops-bot): note: we have an internal playbook for commit migrations. link: https://internal.redwood/commit-playbook (mock link)
nana (ana): tradeoff note — rate caps (tiered) is much faster to ship and helps PLG growth; reserved is enterprise motion. maybe sequence: ship tiered caps + billing primitives, then reserved as enterprise expansion.
jordan (sales): sequenced approach sounds good; but need a templated offer to close a current deal this week. can we do a manual reserved pilot?
mike (eng): manual pilot OK, we can do a config flag + routing rule for 1 customer; no GA SLA. set expectations.
sarah (finance): pilot contract must have explicit usage terms and no long-term discounts until metrics validate.
kevin (devex): milestone checklist for MVP tiered rate caps: config schema, console slider, docs, metric dashboards, and one integration test. estimate 3 sprints.
nana (ana): launch criteria proposals: - Metrics: <5% failed requests due to routing changes - docs + onboarding in place - sales enablement + pricing sheet - billing tested end-to-end.
jordan (sales): I'll take ownership of pilot deal wording; will sync with legal.
mike (eng): I'll scope the minimal config to support manual reserved pilot and the tiered rate caps.
sarah (finance): I'll draft commit pricing guardrails and refund policy.
kevin (devex): I'll write the onboarding checklist and example terraform snippet for reserved binding: ```yaml
reserved_binding:
  org_id: x-123
  pool_id: r-2026
  commit_tokens: 500000
```
nana (ana): agree on sequencing: 1) tiered rate caps (fast), 2) manual reserved pilot (sales-critical), 3) GA reserved with console + SLA. we should revisit RICE after engineering scoping.
jordan (sales): ping @ana for pilot contract language later today.
mike (eng): dropping a TODO: add fallback routing to cheaper model variant when reserved pool saturated. low-risk.
sarah (finance): +1 to fallback — protects margin.
kevin (devex): small UX ask: show projected monthly burn vs commit savings on purchase flow. big impact for conversions.
nana (ops-bot): reminder: create ticket for metrics "reserved_pool_utilization" and alert if <20% or >95%.
nana (ana): thanks all. outcome: sequence approved in thread, owners assigned. will put in roadmap doc and product PRD draft.
